\section{Results}
The end-to-end path has four stages, and every stage
contributes to the tail. Figure~\ref{fig:pipeline} marks
the stages at which we injected additional logging.

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\fbox{\parbox[c][5cm][c]{0.7\textwidth}{\centering pipeline
diagram pending}}
\caption{The serving pipeline from request admission to
response flush.\label{fig:pipeline}}
\end{figure}

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\fbox{\parbox[c][5cm][c]{0.7\textwidth}{\centering latency
heat map pending}}
\caption{Tail latency under staged load, aggregated per
stage.\label{fig:latency}}
\end{figure}

The admission queue dominates the tail above the 99th
percentile, as Figure~\ref{fig:latency} makes clear: queue
wait accounts for nearly two thirds of the worst decile of
requests once the batch aggregator saturates. The model
workers, by contrast, contribute a stable share at every
load level we tested, which suggests that further worker
scaling would buy little until the queue is re-engineered.
